overview: The Account Aggregator (AA) framework is an RBI-approved initiative under India's Digital Public Infrastructure that enables secure, consent-driven sharing of financial data between Financial Information Providers (FIPs) and Financial Information Users (FIUs) via Account Aggregators (AAs). It empowers individuals and businesses to access financial services like loans, insurance, and wealth management by providing real-time, verified financial data with explicit user consent. The framework promotes financial inclusion, reduces operational friction, and supports innovation across lending, investments, insurance, and personal finance sectors. Sahamati acts as the industry body driving adoption, setting standards, and enabling interoperability within the AA ecosystem.
objectives: Enable secure, consent-driven sharing of financial data across financial institutions
Promote financial inclusion by expanding access to credit for underserved and first-time borrowers
Improve efficiency in lending, insurance, and wealth management through real-time data access
Strengthen fraud mitigation and operational efficiency for financial service providers
Support innovation in financial products and services using aggregated financial insights
Ensure data privacy and user control over personal financial information
Establish standardized protocols and fair use templates for responsible data usage
Drive adoption of Account Aggregator ecosystem as a foundational pillar of India's Digital Public Infrastructure
eligibility: Any registered and regulated entity under RBI, PFRDA, SEBI, IRDAI, or Department of Revenue (GSTN) can participate in the AA ecosystem.
benefits: The Account Aggregator framework enables secure, consent-based sharing of financial data, eliminating the need for physical document collection or sharing login credentials. It accelerates credit decisions, reduces operational friction, and expands access to affordable credit, especially for first-time and underserved borrowers. In lending, it improves underwriting accuracy and reduces fraud. In insurance, it enables faster policy issuance, better risk pricing, and improved persistency. In wealth management, it provides holistic financial insights and personalized advisory services. For individuals, it offers a unified, real-time view of finances across accounts, supporting better financial decision-making. The framework ensures data encryption, user-controlled consent management, and prevents data misuse or storage by AAs. It supports interoperability through standardized APIs and certification frameworks, and enables monitoring of government schemes, employee compliance, and counterparty risks. Participants benefit from access to Sahamati’s technical services, Central Registry, dispute resolution, and collaborative governance forums.
financial_support: The Account Aggregator framework does not provide direct financial support such as grants, loans, or subsidies to entities. It is a technological and regulatory infrastructure enabling consent-driven data exchange. Financial benefits accrue indirectly through improved access to credit, reduced processing costs, and enhanced service delivery for participating institutions (FIPs, FIUs, AAs). There is no fund corpus or per-entity financial allocation under the framework itself. Revenue models for participants are based on their respective business models (e.g., AAs may charge transaction fees, FIPs/FIUs gain efficiency). Sahamati generates revenue through membership fees from Regulated Entities (REs), categorized by asset size or revenue tiers.
application_process: 1. Get registered and regulated by at least one Financial Service Regulator (RBI, SEBI, IRDAI, PFRDA). 2. Implement the required module (FIP, FIU, or AA) using RBI-defined API specifications published by ReBIT. 3. Test the module in RBI-approved Account Aggregator Sandboxes. 4. Enrol the module in the UAT-Central Registry for testing in the development environment. 5. Obtain certification from a Sahamati-empanelled auditor for adherence to ReBIT Technical Standards. 6. Get details publicised in the Central Registry upon going live. 7. Launch services with customers. 8. For Regulated Entity (RE) membership in Sahamati: submit valid registration certificate, executed Membership Terms, authorization document, and proof of certification; pay applicable annual fee based on entity category.
required_documents: Valid certificate of registration issued by a financial sector regulator
Duly executed copy of the Sahamati Membership Terms
Copy of the authorisation document in favour of the signatory
Proof of certification as per Sahamati Certification Guidelines
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) in collaboration with Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA), Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority (IRDAI), and Financial Stability Development Council (FSDC)
contact_details: Email: memberservices@sahamati.org.in | For certification: certifier@sahamati.org.in | For Fair Use: fairuse@sahamati.org.in | For SaaNS access: memberservices@sahamati.org.in | For RE membership: membership@sahamati.org.in
caveats: Account Aggregators cannot store, process, or sell customer data
Data sharing is only possible with explicit user consent
Only asset-based data (bank accounts, deposits, mutual funds, insurance, pension funds) is currently accessible
Entities must obtain certification to ensure interoperability and adherence to ReBIT standards
RE membership in Sahamati requires being 'Live' or 'Ready to go Live' in the AA production environment
All NBFC-AAs are classified under Fee Category B for Sahamati membership
Certain entities like AD-II, CRA, PoP, Research Analyst, AIF, TReDS, Cooperative Bank, Depository, PPI Issuer, RRB, and AIFIs are classified under Fee Category C
Token refresh API migration deadlines apply (e.g., old Token APIs discontinued effective 21st August 2025)
V1 API endpoint URLs in Central Registry were deprecated and required migration to V2 by 30th June 2024
RRB amalgamation effective 15th September 2025 requires CR updates: transferor RRBs to be deleted, transferees to update names
Sahamati SahAAyak portal undergoes scheduled downtime for upgrades (e.g., May 18th, 2026, 5:00 PM–10:00 PM IST)
Fair Use Template implementation rules are updated periodically; entities must align with latest versions (e.g., v1.2 effective February 10, 2026)
Consent validity limits for lending use cases are capped (e.g., CT003: up to 5 years; CT035: up to 8 years in defaulter cases)
